headerBody: A port-day defense manual for cruise passengers — 31 scam chapters, the seven port-day pressure patterns, 15 port risk cards from Nassau to Istanbul, eight short drills, and a phrasebook in Spanish, Italian, Greek and Turkish. Built for the few hours you have ashore before the ship leaves.
quadHead: The scams waiting at the bottom of the gangway.

quad.title: The Bird-Poop Splash
quad.tl: Something wet hits your shoulder near La Rambla; a “helpful” stranger appears within seconds with tissues while an accomplice empties your bag. The “bird poop” is mustard squirted from a hidden bottle.

quad.title: Gondola Price Gouging
quad.tl: “€50, nice tour” turns into a 20-minute back-canal loop, then a higher bill — the city's fixed rate is €80 for 30 minutes (€100 after 7pm), only from licensed stations.

quad.title: The Athinios Port 'Public Bus'
quad.tl: High-vis-vest recruiters meet the Piraeus ferry at Athinios Port shouting "Public bus this way! €15 to Fira!" to disoriented arrivals — the real KTEL Santorini bus charges €2.40 for the same route and sits parked at the far end of the terminal in blue-and-white livery. Walk past the loudest voices; anything over €5 for a public-bus seat is the scam.

quad.title: The Fake Police ID Check
quad.tl: Two men near the Grand Bazaar flash laminated badges, claim a counterfeit-currency check, separate your passport from your wallet — and hand the passport back short of cash.

body: The Cruise Passenger Scam Guide is a port-day defense manual — written for the handful of hours you spend ashore, when the clock to the all-aboard is the scammer's best weapon.

Thirty-one scam chapters, the seven port-day pressure patterns, and 15 port risk cards from Nassau to Istanbul — the exact scripts, the red flags, and a phrasebook in Spanish, Italian, Greek and Turkish you can show on your phone.
Re-researched and updated every year — when a new edition ships, it appears in your Kindle library. Walk down the gangway knowing exactly how the port works.
